themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked 900% this week (5 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), with concurrent spikes in asbestos (700% up, 3 complaints 2 weeks ago) and flooring/stairs violations (600% up, 7 complaints 3 weeks ago), suggesting a cluster of serious structural or safety issues affecting multiple properties in Lower Manhattan.
evidence: Building/Use violations up 900% (5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average; z-score 9.0)
Asbestos complaints up 700% (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average; z-score 5.42)
Flooring/Stairs violations up 600% (7 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average; z-score 8.49)
1,131 total DOB permit filings in last 90 days, with 967 alterations—many may relate to failing infrastructure
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings are generating the spike in complaints and interview affected residents about safety concerns
Investigate whether the surge correlates with recent construction activity or aging building stock in the Financial District/Lower East Side areas
Examine whether DOB is keeping pace with inspection and enforcement given the 1,131 permit filings

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints nearly doubled this week (167 complaints vs. 76.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks, a 119% spike with z-score 4.16), while Mobile Food Vendor complaints spiked 700% last week (4 vs. 0.5 average), and Park Rules violations jumped 567% (5 vs. 0.8 average)—indicating enforcement failures or operator surge in public spaces.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement complaints up 119% this week (167 complaints vs. 76.4 weekly average; z-score 4.16)
Mobile Food Vendor complaints up 700% last week (4 vs. 0.5 average; z-score 4.95)
Park Rules violations up 567% last week (5 vs. 0.8 average; z-score 4.39)
Vendor Enforcement is the top complaint category overall (1,234 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Identify hotspots where unlicensed food vendors or non-compliant vendors are concentrated (parks, street corners, transit hubs)
Interview Department of Health and Parks Enforcement about staffing, inspection frequency, and whether recent policy changes have reduced enforcement capacity
Talk to residents and business owners about how vendor issues (illegal parking, trash, permit violations) are degrading quality of life

themes_detail.label: Plumbing & Water Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Heat/Hot Water complaints (243 over 90 days) remain a chronic issue, while Plumbing complaints specifically spiked 361% three weeks ago (19 complaints vs. 4.1 weekly average, z-score 5.31), suggesting a widespread infrastructure failure affecting multiple buildings' water systems in the district.
evidence: Plumbing complaints up 361% (19 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.1 weekly average; z-score 5.31)
Heat/Hot Water remains top-10 complaint category with 243 complaints over 90 days
Community Board has repeated budget requests for 'Other programs to address public health issues'—indicating chronic utilities/habitability failures
reporting_angles: Investigate which specific buildings generated the plumbing spike and whether they share common ownership, age, or maintenance issues
Interview tenants about duration and frequency of hot water outages and whether landlords are responding to complaints
Examine whether aging water infrastructure in Lower Manhattan (pre-1950s buildings common in this district) is failing at accelerating rates

themes_detail.label: Property Loss & Theft Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Lost Property complaints jumped 121% two weeks ago (8 complaints vs. 3.6 weekly average, z-score 5.11), a moderate spike with limited context but worth monitoring given it often correlates with transit crime or organized theft in commercial districts.
evidence: Lost Property complaints up 121% (8 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.6 weekly average; z-score 5.11)
No Reddit discussions or local news coverage yet, suggesting this is an emerging trend not yet on public radar
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and/or 311 to determine whether lost property complaints correlate with theft, scams, or pickpocketing hotspots
Map complaint locations to identify whether losses are concentrated in transit hubs, parks, or commercial corridors
Interview affected residents/workers about circumstances of loss and whether pattern suggests organized theft
